There is a graph $G_{32}$ on $32$ vertices, built from the Mermin--Peres

 2^{C_{\min}(G_{32})}\ \le\ 6.186983\ldots\ <\ 6.194232\ldots\ \le\ \Sigma(G_{32}).

title: Definition
body_md:
\label[definition]{def:representation}
A \emph{representation} of $G$ is a family $(P_x)_{x\in V(G)}$ of nonzero
orthogonal projections on a Hilbert space such that $P_xP_y=0$ whenever
$x\ne y$ are non-adjacent.  A family of states $(\rho_x)$ is
\emph{compatible with} $G$ if its supports form a representation.
head: environment

label: eq:def-parameter
title: Definition
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
The \emph{entanglement-assisted asymptotic spectrum} $X(\mathcal G,\le_*)$ is the set of maps
$\phi$ from finite graphs to $[0,\infty)$ such that
\[
 \phi(G\sqcup H)=\phi(G)+\phi(H),\quad
 \phi(G\boxtimes H)=\phi(G)\phi(H),\quad
 \phi(K_1)=1,\quad
 G\le_*H\Rightarrow\phi(G)\le\phi(H).
\]
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md:
\label[proposition]{prop:supported}
Let $0\le\alpha\le2$ and $s=1-\alpha$.  Then
\[
 \min_{\rho:\ \operatorname{supp}\rho\subseteq\operatorname{ran} P}D_\alpha(\rho\Vert\sigma)
 =-\log Z_s(\sigma,P),
\]
and the minimum is attained at $\rho=K_s(\sigma,P)/Z_s(\sigma,P)$.
head: environment
name: supported minimization

title: Proof
body_md:
For $\rho$ supported in $P$ we have
$\operatorname{Tr}\rho^\alpha\sigma^s=\operatorname{Tr}\rho^\alpha A$ with $A=P\sigma^sP$, and
$Z_s=\operatorname{Tr} A^{1/s}$ when $s\ne0$.

\emph{Case $0<\alpha<1$.}  Here $s\in(0,1)$.  H\"older's inequality for
Schatten norms gives
$\operatorname{Tr}\rho^\alpha A\le\lVert \rho^\alpha\rVert_{1/\alpha}\lVert A\rVert_{1/s}
=(\operatorname{Tr} A^{1/s})^s$.  Since $\alpha-1<0$, this becomes
$D_\alpha(\rho\Vert\sigma)\ge\frac{s}{\alpha-1}\log Z_s=-\log Z_s$, with
equality at $\rho\propto A^{1/s}$.

\emph{Case $1<\alpha\le2$.}  Now $s\in[-1,0)$ and $A$ is positive definite on
$\operatorname{ran} P$.  Write $A=\sum_ka_k\lvert e_k\rangle\!\langle e_k\rvert$ and $q_k=\langle e_k\rvert\rho\lvert e_k\rangle$, a
probability vector.  Convexity of $t\mapsto t^\alpha$ gives
$\langle e_k\rvert\rho^\alpha\lvert e_k\rangle\ge q_k^\alpha$, so
$\operatorname{Tr}\rho^\alpha A\ge\sum_ka_kq_k^\alpha$.  By H\"older,
\[
 1=\sum_k\bigl(a_k^{1/\alpha}q_k\bigr)a_k^{-1/\alpha}
 \le\Bigl(\sum_ka_kq_k^\alpha\Bigr)^{1/\alpha}
    \Bigl(\sum_ka_k^{1/s}\Bigr)^{(\alpha-1)/\alpha},
\]
using $-1/(\alpha-1)=1/s$.  Hence
$\operatorname{Tr}\rho^\alpha A\ge(\sum_ka_k^{1/s})^{s}=Z_s^s$, and dividing the logarithm
by $\alpha-1>0$ gives $D_\alpha\ge-\log Z_s$.  Equality holds when $\rho$ is
diagonal in $(e_k)$ with $q_k\propto a_k^{1/s}$, that is, at
$\rho\propto A^{1/s}$.

\emph{Case $\alpha=1$.}  On $\operatorname{ran} P$ we have
$\ln K_0=P(\ln\sigma)P$, so $\operatorname{Tr}\rho\ln\sigma=\operatorname{Tr}\rho\ln(K_0/Z_0)+\ln Z_0$ and
$D(\rho\Vert\sigma)=D(\rho\Vert K_0/Z_0)-\log Z_0\ge-\log Z_0$.

\emph{Case $\alpha=0$.}  $\operatorname{Tr}\Pi_\rho\sigma\le\operatorname{Tr} P\sigma=Z_1$, with equality
whenever $\rho$ has full support in $\operatorname{ran} P$.
head: environment

title: Lemma
head: environment
name: flat witnesses

title: Proof
body_md:
With $c=\operatorname{Tr}\Pi\sigma$ we get
$\operatorname{Tr}\rho^\alpha\sigma^{1-\alpha}=c^{-\alpha}\operatorname{Tr}\Pi\sigma=c^{1-\alpha}$, which
gives the claim for $\alpha\ne0,1$.  The two remaining orders are direct.
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md:
\label[proposition]{prop:endpoints}
For every graph $G$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},itemsep=1pt]
\item $\vartheta_0(G)=\vartheta(G)$ \textup{\cite[Theorem~8]{Dalai2013TIT},
\cite[proof of Theorem~5]{DuanWinter2016}},
$\vartheta_1(G)=2^{C_{\min}(G)}$
\textup{\cite{OhyaPetzWatanabe1997,SchumacherWestmoreland2001}} and
$\vartheta_2(G)=\Sigma(G)$;
\item $\alpha\mapsto\vartheta_\alpha(G)$ is nondecreasing on $[0,2]$
\textup{(immediate from the monotonicity of $D_\alpha$ in $\alpha$
\cite{Tomamichel2016})};
\item $\vartheta(G)\le\vartheta_\alpha(G)\le\alpha^*(G)$ for every $\alpha\in[0,2]$; at
$\alpha\in\{0,1,2\}$ these bounds follow from Duan and Winter's
chain~\eqref{eq:dw-chain} \textup{\cite{DuanWinter2016}}.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(i) \emph{Order zero.}  This is Dalai's Theorem~8, which he credits to
Schrijver \cite{Dalai2013TIT}.  Duan and Winter give the same purification
argument in the proof of their Theorem~5 \cite[Section~V]{DuanWinter2016},
and for a pure center the passage from projections to vectors is the
argument of Cabello, Severini and Winter \cite[proof of Eq.~(6)]{CSW2010}.
We include the short argument in our notation.
By~\eqref{eq:projection-formula},
$1/\vartheta_0(G)=\sup\min_x\operatorname{Tr} P_x\sigma$.  Lov\'asz's definition of $\vartheta$
through the value of an orthonormal representation reads
$1/\vartheta(G)=\sup\min_x|\langle c,u_x\rangle|^2$ over orthonormal
representations $(u_x)$ of $G$ and unit vectors $c$
\cite[Section~II]{Lovasz1979}.  Lov\'asz uses real vectors, but complex ones
give the same value: rephase each $u_x$ so that $\langle c,u_x\rangle\ge0$,
and then realify, $v\mapsto(\operatorname{Re}v,\operatorname{Im}v)$, which
preserves unit length, orthogonality and the values $\langle c,u_x\rangle$.  A
vector representation is a projection representation with $P_x=\lvert u_x\rangle\!\langle u_x\rvert$,
and a faithful approximation of $\lvert c\rangle\!\langle c\rvert$ gives $\vartheta_0\le\vartheta$.  Conversely,
purify $\sigma$ to a unit vector $c\in\mathcal H\otimes\mathcal H'$ and put
$u_x\propto(P_x\otimes I)c$.  Non-adjacent vertices get orthogonal vectors,
and $|\langle c,u_x\rangle|^2=\operatorname{Tr} P_x\sigma$, so $\vartheta\le\vartheta_0$.

\emph{Order one.}  For each compatible family, the Holevo capacity equals the
relative-entropy radius $\min_\sigma\max_xD(\rho_x\Vert\sigma)$
\cite{OhyaPetzWatanabe1997,SchumacherWestmoreland2001}.  Taking the infimum
over families gives $\vartheta_1=2^{C_{\min}}$.

\emph{Order two.}  By~\eqref{eq:projection-formula},
$1/\vartheta_2=\sup\min_x\operatorname{Tr}\sigma_{/P_x}$.  Given a compatible family and $T\ge\rho_x$
with $t=\operatorname{Tr} T$, put $\sigma=T/t$, regularized if needed.  Each $\rho_x/t$ lies
below $\sigma$ with range in $\operatorname{ran} P_x$, so $\operatorname{Tr}\sigma_{/P_x}\ge1/t$.  Hence
$\vartheta_2\le\Sigma$.  Conversely, if $\operatorname{Tr}\sigma_{/P_x}\ge c$ for all $x$, the
states $\rho_x=\sigma_{/P_x}/\operatorname{Tr}\sigma_{/P_x}$ are compatible and all lie below
$T=\sigma/c$, whose trace is $1/c$.  Hence $\Sigma\le\vartheta_2$.

(ii) $D_\alpha$ is nondecreasing in $\alpha$ for each pair of states, and
infima preserve this.

(iii) The lower bound follows from (i) and (ii).  The upper bound also
follows from (i), (ii) and~\eqref{eq:dw-chain}, since
$\vartheta_\alpha\le\vartheta_2=\Sigma\le\alpha^*$; flat witnesses give it directly.
Take a
fractional clique cover $w$ with $\sum_Cw_C=\alpha^*(G)$, and work on the
space spanned by orthonormal vectors $\lvert C\rangle$, one for each clique with
$w_C>0$.  Put $\sigma=\sum_Cw_C\lvert C\rangle\!\langle C\rvert/\alpha^*(G)$ and let $\Pi_x$ project
onto the cliques containing $x$.  Non-adjacent vertices share no clique, so the
flat states $\rho_x=\Pi_x\sigma/\operatorname{Tr}\Pi_x\sigma$ are compatible.  By
\cref{lem:flat} their radius at every order is
$\max_x\log\bigl(\alpha^*(G)/\sum_{C\ni x}w_C\bigr)\le\log\alpha^*(G)$.
head: environment

title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md:
\label[proposition]{prop:sandwiched}
For every graph $G$ and every $\beta\in[\frac12,\infty]$,
\[
 \widetilde\vartheta_\beta(G)=\vartheta_{2-1/\beta}(G),
\]
with $2-1/\infty=2$.  In particular,
\[
 \widetilde\vartheta_{1/2}=\vartheta,\qquad
 \widetilde\vartheta_{2/3}=\vartheta_{1/2},\qquad
 \widetilde\vartheta_1=2^{C_{\min}},\qquad
 \widetilde\vartheta_\infty=\Sigma.
\]
head: environment
name: sandwiched radii

label: eq:sandwiched-supported
title: Proof
body_md:
Put $s=(1-\beta)/\beta\in[-1,1]$, with $s=-1$ at $\beta=\infty$, so the
corresponding Petz order is $\alpha=1-s=2-1/\beta$.  As in the proof
of~\eqref{eq:projection-formula}, it suffices to show that for a projection
$P\ne0$ and a faithful state $\sigma$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sandwiched-supported}
 \min_{\rho:\ \operatorname{supp}\rho\subseteq\operatorname{ran} P}\widetilde D_\beta(\rho\Vert\sigma)
 =-\log Z_s(\sigma,P),
\end{equation}
with a minimizer faithful on $\operatorname{ran} P$.  All inverses and compressed powers
below are taken on $\operatorname{ran} P$.

\emph{Case $\frac12\le\beta<1$.}  Here $s\in(0,1]$.  Put
$A=P\sigma^sP>0$ on $\operatorname{ran} P$ and $X=A^{1/2}\rho A^{1/2}$.  The constraint
on $\rho$ becomes $X\ge0$, $\operatorname{Tr} A^{-1}X=1$.  The map
$V=\sigma^{s/2}P A^{-1/2}:\operatorname{ran} P\to\mathcal H$ is an isometry, and
\[
 \sigma^{s/2}\rho\sigma^{s/2}=VXV^*.
\]
Consequently the sandwiched moment is $\operatorname{Tr} X^\beta$.
Pinch $X$ in an orthonormal eigenbasis $(e_i)$ of $A$, obtaining $Y$.
Pinching preserves $\operatorname{Tr} A^{-1}X$ and cannot decrease $\operatorname{Tr} X^\beta$:
it is an average of unitary conjugations, and $X\mapsto\operatorname{Tr} X^\beta$ is
concave for $0<\beta<1$.  Writing $Ae_i=a_i e_i$ and
$\langle e_i,Ye_i\rangle=a_iq_i$, we have $q_i\ge0$ and $\sum_iq_i=1$.
Scalar H\"older with conjugate exponents $1/\beta$ and $1/(1-\beta)$ gives
\[
 \operatorname{Tr} X^\beta\le\operatorname{Tr} Y^\beta
 =\sum_i a_i^\beta q_i^\beta
 \le\Bigl(\sum_i a_i^{\beta/(1-\beta)}\Bigr)^{1-\beta}
 =Z_s(\sigma,P)^{1-\beta}.
\]
Equality holds at $\rho=A^{1/s}/Z_s=K_s/Z_s$:
then $q_i=a_i^{1/s}/Z_s$ and $X$ is already diagonal in $(e_i)$.
Since $\beta-1<0$, maximizing the moment minimizes the divergence, giving
\eqref{eq:sandwiched-supported}.  At $\beta=\frac12$ this directly reads
$-\log Z_1(\sigma,P)=-\log\operatorname{Tr} P\sigma$; no limiting argument is needed.

\emph{Case $\beta=1$.}  This is Proposition~\ref{prop:supported} at order
one, with minimizer $K_0/Z_0$.

\emph{Case $1<\beta<\infty$.}  Put $\theta=(\beta-1)/\beta\in(0,1)$,
so $s=-\theta$, and let $A=P\sigma^{-\theta}P$, which is positive
definite on $\operatorname{ran} P$, and $X=A^{1/2}\rho A^{1/2}$.  The operator
$\sigma^{-\theta/2}\rho\,\sigma^{-\theta/2}$ has the same nonzero eigenvalues
as $\rho^{1/2}\sigma^{-\theta}\rho^{1/2}=\rho^{1/2}A\rho^{1/2}$, and hence as
$X$, so the sandwiched moment is $\operatorname{Tr} X^\beta$.  Since
$\operatorname{Tr} A^{-1}X=\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$, H\"older's inequality with the conjugate exponents
$\beta$ and $\beta/(\beta-1)=1/\theta$ gives
\[
 1\le\lVert X\rVert_\beta\,\lVert A^{-1}\rVert_{1/\theta}
 =\bigl(\operatorname{Tr} X^\beta\bigr)^{1/\beta}\bigl(\operatorname{Tr} A^{-1/\theta}\bigr)^{\theta}.
\]
Here $A^{-1/\theta}=(P\sigma^{-\theta}P)^{1/(-\theta)}=K_{-\theta}(\sigma,P)$,
so $\operatorname{Tr} X^\beta\ge Z_{-\theta}(\sigma,P)^{-(\beta-1)}$, which is the lower bound
in~\eqref{eq:sandwiched-supported}.  At $\rho=K_{-\theta}/Z_{-\theta}$ we get
$X\propto A^{1-1/\theta}$, so $X^\beta\propto A^{-1/\theta}=(A^{-1})^{1/\theta}$,
which is the equality case of H\"older's inequality.

\emph{Case $\beta=\infty$.}  The condition $\rho\le\lambda\sigma$ for a state
supported in $\operatorname{ran} P$ says that $\rho/\lambda$ lies below $\sigma$ with
range in $\operatorname{ran} P$, so
$1/\lambda\le\operatorname{Tr}\sigma_{/P}=Z_{-1}(\sigma,P)$, with equality at
$\rho=\sigma_{/P}/\operatorname{Tr}\sigma_{/P}=K_{-1}/Z_{-1}$.

In every case $K_s/Z_s$ is faithful on $\operatorname{ran} P$.  Thus the minimizing
states retain the prescribed supports, and for a graph with at least one
vertex the same
argument as in~\eqref{eq:projection-formula} yields
\[
 \frac1{\widetilde\vartheta_\beta(G)}
 =\sup_{(P_x),\,\sigma}\min_x Z_s(\sigma,P_x)
 =\frac1{\vartheta_{1-s}(G)}.
\]
The null graph follows from the conventions.  These identities hold in
each fixed dimension before optimizing over representations and centers;
no exchange of an order limit with an unbounded-dimension infimum is used.
head: environment

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label[lemma]{lem:tower}
Let $P\le Q$ be projections and $s\in[-1,1]$.  Compute the outer compression
below inside $\operatorname{ran} Q$, where $K_s(\sigma,Q)$ is faithful.  Then
\[
 K_s\bigl(K_s(\sigma,Q),P\bigr)=K_s(\sigma,P).
\]
Consequently, if $z=Z_s(\sigma,Q)$, then
$Z_s\bigl(K_s(\sigma,Q)/z,\,P\bigr)=Z_s(\sigma,P)/z$.
head: environment
name: tower identity

title: Proof
body_md:
For $s\ne0$, the $s$-th power of $K_s(\sigma,Q)$ inside $\operatorname{ran} Q$ is
$Q\sigma^sQ$, and compressing further to $P\le Q$ gives $P\sigma^sP$.  For
$s=0$ the same computation works with logarithms.  The second statement
follows from homogeneity.
head: environment

label: thm:product
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:product}
For $0\le\alpha\le2$ and all graphs $G,H$,
\[
 \vartheta_\alpha(G\boxtimes H)=\vartheta_\alpha(G)\,\vartheta_\alpha(H).
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If either graph is the null graph both sides vanish, so assume that both
have vertices and put $s=1-\alpha$.

For ``$\le$'', take witnesses $(\rho_x),\sigma$ for $G$ and $(\tau_y),\omega$
for $H$.  If $(x,y)$ and $(x',y')$ are distinct and non-adjacent in $G\boxtimes H$,
then $x,x'$ are distinct and non-adjacent in $G$ or $y,y'$ are in $H$.  In
either case $(\rho_x\otimes\tau_y)(\rho_{x'}\otimes\tau_{y'})=0$.  Since
$D_\alpha$ is additive under tensor products, radii add.

For ``$\ge$'', let $(P_{xy})$ represent $G\boxtimes H$, let $\sigma$ be faithful,
and suppose $Z_s(\sigma,P_{xy})\ge c>0$ for every pair $(x,y)$.  Let $S_x$ be
the projection onto $\sum_y\operatorname{ran} P_{xy}$, and put $z_x=Z_s(\sigma,S_x)$.

\emph{The rows represent $G$.}  If $x\ne x'$ are non-adjacent in $G$, every
pair $(x,y),(x',y')$ is distinct and non-adjacent in $G\boxtimes H$, so
$P_{xy}P_{x'y'}=0$ and hence $S_xS_{x'}=0$.

\emph{Each row represents $H$.}  Fix $x$.  If $y\ne y'$ are non-adjacent in
$H$, then $(x,y)$ and $(x,y')$ are non-adjacent, so $(P_{xy})_y$ represents
$H$ on $\operatorname{ran} S_x$.  Use the faithful state $\sigma_x=K_s(\sigma,S_x)/z_x$ on
$\operatorname{ran} S_x$ as center.  By \cref{lem:tower},
$Z_s(\sigma_x,P_{xy})=Z_s(\sigma,P_{xy})/z_x\ge c/z_x$ for every $y$.  The
projection formula~\eqref{eq:projection-formula} for $H$ gives
$c/z_x\le1/\vartheta_\alpha(H)$, that is, $z_x\ge c\,\vartheta_\alpha(H)$.

\emph{Combine.}  Apply~\eqref{eq:projection-formula} for $G$ to $(S_x)$ and
$\sigma$: $c\,\vartheta_\alpha(H)\le\min_xz_x\le1/\vartheta_\alpha(G)$.  So
$c\le1/(\vartheta_\alpha(G)\vartheta_\alpha(H))$ for every admissible $c$, and taking the
supremum gives
\[
 \frac1{\vartheta_\alpha(G\boxtimes H)}\le\frac1{\vartheta_\alpha(G)\,\vartheta_\alpha(H)} .
 \qedhere
\]
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
\label[remark]{rem:single-letter}
At $\alpha=0$ and $\alpha=1$, \cref{thm:product} recovers the multiplicativity
of $\vartheta$ \cite{Lovasz1979} and Duan and Winter's additivity of $C_{\min}$
\cite[Lemma~23]{DuanWinter2016}.  At $\alpha=2$ it says
$\Sigma(G\boxtimes H)=\Sigma(G)\Sigma(H)$.
Hence $S_{0,\mathrm{NS}}(G)=\log\Sigma(G)$: regularizing the graph-level value
$\log\Sigma(G)$, an infimum of one-shot SDP costs, does not change it.  Their
fixed-cq-graph multiplicativity \cite[Proposition~18]{DuanWinter2016} gives
this identity only for the infimum restricted to product representations
$P_{xy}=P_x\otimes Q_y$.  \Cref{thm:product} removes that restriction, but it
does not recover their statement for fixed cq-graphs.
head: environment

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label[lemma]{lem:compression}
Let $Q\ne0$ be a projection, $s=1-\alpha\in[-1,1]$, and
$\sigma_Q=K_s(\sigma,Q)/Z_s(\sigma,Q)$.  Every state $\rho$ supported in
$\operatorname{ran} Q$ satisfies
\[
 D_\alpha(\rho\Vert\sigma)=D_\alpha(\rho\Vert\sigma_Q)-\log Z_s(\sigma,Q).
\]
head: environment
name: compression identity

title: Proof
body_md:
For $\alpha\notin\{0,1\}$, substitute $Q\sigma^sQ=Z_s^s\sigma_Q^s$ into the
Petz moment.  For $\alpha=1$ use $Q(\ln\sigma)Q=\ln\sigma_Q+(\ln Z_0)Q$ on
$\operatorname{ran} Q$, and for $\alpha=0$ use $Q\sigma Q=Z_1\sigma_Q$.
head: environment

title: Lemma
head: environment
name: orthogonal blocks

label: thm:union
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:union}
For $0\le\alpha\le2$, $\vartheta_\alpha(G\sqcup H)=\vartheta_\alpha(G)+\vartheta_\alpha(H)$.
head: environment
name: disjoint unions

title: Proof
body_md:
Assume that neither graph is the null graph.  For ``$\le$'', put witnesses
for $G$ and $H$
with radii at most $\log a$ and $\log b$ on orthogonal summands, and use the
center $(a\sigma_G\oplus b\sigma_H)/(a+b)$.  Compressing this center to the
first summand gives weight $a/(a+b)$ and reduced center $\sigma_G$, so by
\cref{lem:compression} every $G$-state has radius at most
$\log a+\log\frac{a+b}{a}=\log(a+b)$.  The same holds for $H$.

For ``$\ge$'', take a compatible family of $G\sqcup H$ with center $\sigma$
and radius at most $R$.  Let $Q_G$ and $Q_H$ project onto the spans of the
supports of the two subfamilies.  Cross pairs are non-adjacent, so
$Q_GQ_H=0$.  By \cref{lem:compression}, the $G$-states have radius at most
$R+\log Z_s(\sigma,Q_G)$ around $\sigma_{Q_G}$, so
$\vartheta_\alpha(G)\le2^RZ_s(\sigma,Q_G)$.  Likewise
$\vartheta_\alpha(H)\le2^RZ_s(\sigma,Q_H)$.  Add the two bounds and apply
\cref{lem:orthogonal-sum}.
head: environment

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label[lemma]{lem:flagged}
Let $\omega_h\ge0$ with $\sum_h\omega_h=\omega$ and $\operatorname{Tr}\omega=1$, let
$\tau_h$ be states and let $\sigma$ be faithful.  If
$D_\alpha(\tau_h\Vert\sigma)\le R$ whenever $\omega_h\ne0$, then for
$0\le\alpha\le2$
\[
 D_\alpha\Bigl(\sum_h\omega_h\otimes\tau_h\ \Big\Vert\ \omega\otimes\sigma\Bigr)\le R .
\]
head: environment
name: flagged mixtures

title: Proof
body_md:
Add a classical flag and compare
$\Omega=\sum_h\lvert h\rangle\!\langle h\rvert\otimes\omega_h\otimes\tau_h$ with
$\Omega'=\sum_h\lvert h\rangle\!\langle h\rvert\otimes\omega_h\otimes\sigma$; the support of $\Omega$
lies in that of $\Omega'$.  The Petz moment splits over the flag, and the
$\omega_h$ factors cancel:
\[
 \operatorname{Tr}\Omega^\alpha\Omega'^{1-\alpha}=\sum_hw_h\operatorname{Tr}\tau_h^\alpha\sigma^{1-\alpha},
 \qquad w_h=\operatorname{Tr}\omega_h,\ \ \textstyle\sum_hw_h=1.
\]
For $0<\alpha<1$ each term satisfies
$\operatorname{Tr}\tau_h^\alpha\sigma^{1-\alpha}\ge2^{(\alpha-1)R}$, so the average does too
and $D_\alpha(\Omega\Vert\Omega')\le R$.  For $1<\alpha\le2$ all inequalities
reverse and the conclusion is the same.  At $\alpha=1$ the divergence is the
$w$-average of the $D(\tau_h\Vert\sigma)$, and at $\alpha=0$ we get
$\operatorname{Tr}\Pi_\Omega\Omega'=\sum_hw_h\operatorname{Tr}\Pi_{\tau_h}\sigma\ge2^{-R}$.  Tracing out
the flag maps $\Omega\mapsto\sum_h\omega_h\otimes\tau_h$ and
$\Omega'\mapsto\omega\otimes\sigma$, and Petz divergences of order
$\alpha\in[0,2]$ do not increase under partial traces
\cite{Petz1986,Tomamichel2016}.
head: environment

label: thm:ea-mono
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:ea-mono}
If $G\le_*H$, then $\vartheta_\alpha(G)\le\vartheta_\alpha(H)$ for every $\alpha\in[0,2]$.
head: environment
name: entanglement-assisted monotonicity

title: Proof
body_md:
If $G$ is the null graph there is nothing to prove, and otherwise
\eqref{eq:ea-sum} forces $H$ to have a vertex.  Take $\omega,\omega_g^h$ as
in~\eqref{eq:ea-sum}--\eqref{eq:ea-orth}, restricted to $\operatorname{supp}\omega$, and a
compatible family $(\tau_h)$ for $H$ with faithful center $\sigma$ and radius
at most $R$.  Define
\[
 \tau'_g=\sum_h\omega_g^h\otimes\tau_h,\qquad \sigma'=\omega\otimes\sigma .
\]
Each $\tau'_g$ has trace $\operatorname{Tr}\omega=1$.  If $g\ne g'$ are non-adjacent, every
term of $\tau'_g\tau'_{g'}=\sum_{h,h'}\omega_g^h\omega_{g'}^{h'}\otimes\tau_h\tau_{h'}$
vanishes.  When $h\simeq h'$ this is~\eqref{eq:ea-orth}.  Otherwise $h,h'$
are distinct and non-adjacent in $H$, and then $\tau_h\tau_{h'}=0$.  So
$(\tau'_g)$ is compatible with $G$, and \cref{lem:flagged} bounds its radius
around $\sigma'$ by $R$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Normalization was noted at the start of the section.  Additivity is
\cref{thm:union}, multiplicativity is \cref{thm:product}, and monotonicity is
\cref{thm:ea-mono}.  At $\alpha=0$ these are properties of $\vartheta$, and
membership of $\vartheta$ in $X(\mathcal G,\le_*)$ is Li and Zuiddam's theorem
\cite{LiZuiddam2020}, whose monotonicity step is due to Cubitt et
al.~\cite{CMRSSW2014}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
\label[remark]{rem:above-two}
The only place the restriction $\alpha\le2$ enters is data processing in
\cref{lem:flagged}.  \Cref{prop:supported}, \cref{lem:tower} and
\cref{lem:compression,lem:orthogonal-sum} hold verbatim for $s<-1$, that is,
for $\alpha>2$, so data processing is the only obstruction in this argument.
Petz data processing fails above order two, and the inequality of
\cref{lem:flagged} itself fails too: the accompanying verification scripts
(see Data and code availability) exhibit an explicit finite-dimensional
instance at order three in which it fails by more than half a bit.  So this
argument says nothing about $\alpha>2$.
head: environment
name: orders above two

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label[lemma]{lem:hs}
For every representation of $C_5$ and every operator $X$,
\[
 \sum_i\lVert P_iXP_i\rVert_2^2\le2\lVert X\rVert_2^2 .
\]
head: environment
name: Hilbert--Schmidt inequality

label: eq:PTP
title: Proof
body_md:
Put $T=\sum_iP_i$.  The terms $P_iP_{i\pm2}P_i$ vanish, and $P_{i-1}$ and
$P_{i+1}$ are orthogonal to each other, so
\begin{equation}\label{eq:PTP}
 P_iTP_i=P_i+P_i(P_{i-1}+P_{i+1})P_i\le2P_i .
\end{equation}
Consider the map $\mathcal A:(X_i)_i\mapsto\sum_iX_i$ from
$\bigoplus_iP_i\mathcal B_2P_i$ to the Hilbert--Schmidt class $\mathcal B_2$.
For $X_i=P_iX_iP_i$, cyclicity gives
$\operatorname{Tr} X_i^*X_j=\operatorname{Tr}\bigl((P_jX_i)^*(X_jP_i)\bigr)$, so
\[
 |\operatorname{Tr} X_i^*X_j|\le\tfrac12\bigl(\lVert P_jX_i\rVert_2^2+\lVert X_jP_i\rVert_2^2\bigr).
\]
Summing over $i$ and $j$ and using~\eqref{eq:PTP},
\[
 \Bigl\lVert\sum_iX_i\Bigr\rVert_2^2
 \le\tfrac12\sum_i\bigl[\operatorname{Tr}(X_i^*TX_i)+\operatorname{Tr}(X_iTX_i^*)\bigr]
 \le2\sum_i\lVert X_i\rVert_2^2 .
\]
So $\lVert \mathcal A\rVert^2\le2$.  The adjoint of $\mathcal A$ is
$X\mapsto(P_iXP_i)_i$, and it has the same norm.
head: environment

label: thm:pentagon-half
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:pentagon-half}
$\vartheta_\alpha(C_5)=\frac52$ for every $\alpha\in[\frac12,2]$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
At $s=\frac12$ the weight is $Z_{1/2}(\sigma,P)=\lVert P\sigma^{1/2}P\rVert_2^2$.
\Cref{lem:hs} with $X=\sigma^{1/2}$ gives
$\sum_iZ_{1/2}(\sigma,P_i)\le2\operatorname{Tr}\sigma=2$.  So the minimum over $i$ is at
most $\frac25$, and~\eqref{eq:projection-formula} gives
$\vartheta_{1/2}(C_5)\ge\frac52$.  By monotonicity in $\alpha$ the same lower bound
holds on $[\frac12,2]$.  For the upper bound, $\alpha^*(C_5)=\frac52$ and
\cref{prop:endpoints}(iii) applies.  Explicitly, the flat witness is
$\rho_i=\frac12(\lvert i\rangle\!\langle i\rvert+\lvert i+1\rangle\!\langle i+1\rvert)$ on $\mathbb C^5$ with $\sigma=I/5$, and
it has radius $\log\frac52$ at every order.
head: environment

title: Lemma
head: environment
name: trace-norm inequality

title: Proof
body_md:
If $(P_i)$ represents $G$ and $v$ is a vector, pick unit vectors
$u_i\in\operatorname{ran} P_i$ parallel to $P_iv$ (arbitrary if $P_iv=0$).  They form an
orthonormal representation of $G$, and $\sum_i\lVert P_iv\rVert^2=\sum_i|\langle
u_i,v\rangle|^2\le\vartheta(\overline G)\lVert v\rVert^2$ by Lov\'asz's Theorem~5 applied
to $\overline G$ \cite{Lovasz1979}.  That theorem is stated for real vectors;
to apply it, rephase each $u_i$ so that $\langle u_i,v\rangle\ge0$ and
realify, $w\mapsto(\operatorname{Re}w,\operatorname{Im}w)$, which preserves
unit length, orthogonality and the values $\langle u_i,v\rangle$.  The
pentagon is self-complementary, so the constant is
$\sqrt5$.  For $X=ab^*$ we have $\lVert P_iab^*P_i\rVert_1=\lVert P_ia\rVert\lVert P_ib\rVert$, and
Cauchy--Schwarz proves the claim for rank one.  A singular value decomposition
and the triangle inequality do the rest.
head: environment

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label[lemma]{lem:interp}
For $1\le p\le2$, every representation of $C_5$ and every operator $X$,
\[
 \sum_i\lVert P_iXP_i\rVert_p^p\le B(p)\,\lVert X\rVert_p^p,
 \qquad B(p)=5^{(2-p)/2}\,2^{p-1}.
\]
head: environment
name: interpolation

title: Proof
body_md:
Consider the map $T:X\mapsto\bigoplus_iP_iXP_i$ into block-diagonal
operators on $\mathbb C^5\otimes\mathcal H$.  For block-diagonal operators
$\lVert \bigoplus_iY_i\rVert_p^p=\sum_i\lVert Y_i\rVert_p^p$, so the claim says that $T$
has norm at most $B(p)^{1/p}$ from $S_p(\mathcal H)$ to $S_p(\mathbb C^5\otimes\mathcal H)$.
By \cref{lem:trace} the norm is at most $\sqrt5$ for $p=1$, and by
\cref{lem:hs} it is at most $\sqrt2$ for $p=2$.  The Schatten classes form a
complex interpolation scale with equal norms \cite[Eq.~(2.1)]{PisierXu2003},
and the complex method is exact of exponent $\theta$
\cite{BerghLofstrom1976}, here $\theta=2-2/p$.  So the norm from $S_p$ to
$S_p$ is at most
$\sqrt5^{\,1-\theta}\sqrt2^{\,\theta}=5^{(2-p)/(2p)}2^{(p-1)/p}$.  Raise this
to the power $p$.
head: environment

label: thm:pentagon-bounds
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For the lower bound put $s=1/p$ and $X=\sigma^s$ in \cref{lem:interp}.  Then
$\lVert X\rVert_p^p=\operatorname{Tr}\sigma=1$ and $\lVert P_i\sigma^sP_i\rVert_p^p=Z_s(\sigma,P_i)$, so
$\sum_iZ_s(\sigma,P_i)\le B(p)$.  The minimum is at most the average, so
$\vartheta_\alpha(C_5)\ge5/B(p)=\sqrt5(\sqrt5/2)^{p-1}$.

The step from the minimum to the average loses nothing.  Given a
representation $(P_i)$ of $C_5$ with center $\sigma$, the projections
$P'_i=\bigoplus_{k\in\mathbb Z_5}P_{i+k}$ on $\mathbb C^5\otimes\mathcal H$ again
represent $C_5$, and with the center $\sigma'=\bigoplus_k\sigma/5$
homogeneity and additivity over orthogonal blocks give
$Z_s(\sigma',P'_i)=\frac15\sum_kZ_s(\sigma,P_k)$ for every $i$.  So the
minimum for $(P'_i)$ and $\sigma'$ is the average for $(P_i)$ and $\sigma$,
and the supremum of the minimum equals the supremum of the average.

The bound $\frac52$ is \cref{thm:pentagon-half} combined with monotonicity.
For the other upper bound, take the umbrella of
\cref{fig:pentagon-geometries}(b): unit vectors
$u_i=(\cos\gamma,\sin\gamma\cos\frac{2\pi i}5,\sin\gamma\sin\frac{2\pi i}5)$
with $\cos^2\gamma=1/\sqrt5$, which satisfy $u_i\perp u_{i+2}$.  For a pure
state, $\operatorname{Tr}\lvert u\rangle\!\langle u\rvert^\alpha\sigma^{1-\alpha}=\langle u\rvert\sigma^{1-\alpha}\lvert u\rangle$.
As faithful centers approach $\lvert c\rangle\!\langle c\rvert$ with $c=(1,0,0)$, this tends to
$|\langle c,u_i\rangle|^2=5^{-1/2}$ because $1-\alpha>0$.  The radius
therefore tends to $\frac{1}{1-\alpha}\log\sqrt5=\log5^{p/2}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The values on $[\frac12,2]$ are \cref{thm:pentagon-half}, and the bounds on
$[0,\frac12]$ are \cref{thm:pentagon-bounds}.  By
\cref{prop:continuity,prop:endpoints}, $\alpha\mapsto\vartheta_\alpha(C_5)$ is
continuous and nondecreasing on $[0,\frac12]$.  It runs from $\vartheta(C_5)=\sqrt5$
to $\frac52$, so by the intermediate value theorem its image is
$[\sqrt5,\frac52]$.  Parameters with different values on $C_5$ are different
functions, and each of them lies in $X(\mathcal G,\le_*)$ by \cref{thm:A}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Readers who want explicit separations without the intermediate value theorem
can use $\alpha_k=1/(8^{k+1}+1)$, $k\ge0$.  Then $p_k-1=8^{-(k+1)}$, and the
bounds~\eqref{eq:pentagon-intro} give
$\vartheta_{\alpha_{k+1}}(C_5)\le\sqrt5\cdot5^{(p_k-1)/16}
<\sqrt5\,(\sqrt5/2)^{p_k-1}\le\vartheta_{\alpha_k}(C_5)$.  The strict inequality is
$5^{1/16}<\sqrt5/2$, that is, $2^{16}=65536<78125=5^7$.  Together with
$\vartheta_{\alpha_0}(C_5)\le5^{9/16}<\frac52$, this shows that
$\vartheta,\vartheta_{\alpha_0},\vartheta_{\alpha_1},\dots,\vartheta_{1/2}$ are pairwise distinct.
head: environment
name: an explicit ladder

title: Corollary
body_md:
\label[corollary]{cor:pentagon}
$\log\sqrt5<C_{\min}(C_5)=S_{0,\mathrm{NS}}(C_5)=\log\Sigma(C_5)=\log\alpha^*(C_5)=\log\frac52$.
head: environment
name: the pentagon conjecture

title: Proof
body_md:
\Cref{thm:pentagon-half,prop:endpoints} give
$C_{\min}(C_5)=\log\Sigma(C_5)=\log\frac52$, and~\eqref{eq:dw-chain} squeezes
$S_{0,\mathrm{NS}}(C_5)$ between them.  The fractional packing number of $C_5$ is
$\frac52$ \cite{Shannon1956} and $\vartheta(C_5)=\sqrt5$ \cite{Lovasz1979}.
head: environment

title: Corollary
head: environment
name: the middle links

title: Proof
body_md:
The first statement is \cref{rem:single-letter}.  The second is
\cref{thm:C}, since $C_{\min}(G_{32})<\log\Sigma(G_{32})=S_{0,\mathrm{NS}}(G_{32})$.
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md:
\label[proposition]{prop:bridge}
For every profile $k$,
\[
 2^{C_{\min}(F[k])}\le\frac1{t_W(F[k])}
 \qquad\text{and}\qquad
 \Sigma(F[k])\ge\frac1{t_H(F[k])} .
\]
head: environment
name: bridge

title: Proof
body_md:
\emph{Upper bound on $C_{\min}$.}  Start from a representation $(P_v)$ of $F$
and a state $\sigma$.  Let $A=\prod_{v:k_v>0}\{1,\dots,k_v\}$, work on
$\bigoplus_{f\in A}\mathcal H$, and put
\[
 \sigma'=\frac1{|A|}\bigoplus_{f\in A}\sigma,\qquad
 P'_{v,a}=\bigoplus_{f\in A:\,f(v)=a}P_v
\]
(zero in the other summands).  Copies of one vertex live in disjoint sets of
summands, so they are orthogonal, and non-adjacent seed vertices stay
orthogonal.  So $(P'_{v,a})$ represents $F[k]$.  Functional calculus on the
direct sum gives $w_{\sigma'}(P'_{v,a})=w_\sigma(P_v)/k_v$.  Now apply the
projection formula~\eqref{eq:projection-formula} at $\alpha=1$ together with
$\vartheta_1=2^{C_{\min}}$.

\emph{Lower bound on $\Sigma$.}  Take a compatible family $(\rho_{v,a})$ for
$F[k]$ and $T\ge\rho_{v,a}$, put $t=\operatorname{Tr} T$ and $\sigma=T/t$ (regularized if
needed), and let $P_{v,a}$ be the supports.  As in
\cref{prop:endpoints}, $h_\sigma(P_{v,a})\ge1/t$.  Copies of one vertex are
non-adjacent, so $P_v=\sum_aP_{v,a}$ is a projection, and $(P_v)$ (with
$P_v=0$ for deleted $v$) represents $F$.  The harmonic weight is
superadditive over orthogonal blocks: for a positive definite block matrix
$M$, each diagonal block of $M^{-1}$ dominates the inverse of the
corresponding block of $M$.  Applied to $M=P_v\sigma^{-1}P_v$ this gives
$h_\sigma(P_v)\ge\sum_ah_\sigma(P_{v,a})\ge k_v/t$.  Hence
$t_H(F[k])\ge1/t$.
head: environment

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label[lemma]{lem:harmonic-moment}
For every $v$,
\[
 (P_v\otimes E_v)\Omega=(I\otimes E_v)\Omega
 \qquad\text{and}\qquad
 \langle\Omega,(I\otimes E_v)\Omega\rangle=h_\sigma(P_v).
\]
head: environment
name: harmonic weight as a moment

title: Proof
body_md:
With $(A\otimes B)\operatorname{vec}(M)=\operatorname{vec}(AMB^{\mathsf T})$, the first identity says
$P_v\sqrt\sigma F_v=\sqrt\sigma F_v$.  This holds because $\sqrt\sigma F_v$
has range $\operatorname{ran} P_v$.  For the second, $\sqrt\sigma F_v\sqrt\sigma$ lies below
$\sigma$ and has range in $\operatorname{ran} P_v$.  If $0\le A\le\sigma$ has range in
$\operatorname{ran} P_v$, then $\sigma^{-1/2}A\sigma^{-1/2}$ is a contraction supported in
$\operatorname{ran} F_v$, hence at most $F_v$.  So
$\sqrt\sigma F_v\sqrt\sigma=\sigma_{/P_v}$, and its trace is the moment.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Combine~\eqref{eq:g32-rationals} with \cref{prop:bridge}.  The reciprocals of
the two rationals, $6.186983\ldots$ and $6.194232\ldots$, are the bounds in
\cref{thm:C}.
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md:
\label[proposition]{prop:bridge-exact}
Let $k$ be a profile with at least one positive entry.  If $(P_v)$ and
$\sigma$ are as in the definition of $t_H(F[k])$, then
\[
 \Sigma(F[k])\le\max_{v:\,k_v>0}\frac{k_v}{h_\sigma(P_v)} .
\]
Consequently $\Sigma(F[k])=1/t_H(F[k])$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $L$ be a common multiple of the positive $k_v$.  On $\mathcal H\otimes\mathbb
C^L$ put $\sigma'=\sigma\otimes I/L$.  For each $v$ with $k_v>0$, split the
standard basis of $\mathbb C^L$ into $k_v$ consecutive blocks of $L/k_v$
vectors, let $\Pi_{v,a}$ project onto the $a$-th block, and put
$P'_{v,a}=P_v\otimes\Pi_{v,a}$.  Copies of one vertex get orthogonal blocks,
and non-adjacent seed vertices have orthogonal $P_v$, so $(P'_{v,a})$
represents $F[k]$.  Since
$P'_{v,a}\sigma'^{-1}P'_{v,a}=P_v\sigma^{-1}P_v\otimes L\,\Pi_{v,a}$, the
shorted operator factorizes, $\sigma'_{/P'_{v,a}}=\sigma_{/P_v}\otimes
\Pi_{v,a}/L$, and
\[
 h_{\sigma'}(P'_{v,a})=h_\sigma(P_v)\,\frac{\operatorname{Tr}\Pi_{v,a}}L=\frac{h_\sigma(P_v)}{k_v}.
\]
The projection formula~\eqref{eq:projection-formula} at $\alpha=2$, with
$\vartheta_2=\Sigma$ (\cref{prop:endpoints}), gives the displayed bound.  Taking
the supremum over $(P_v)$ and $\sigma$ gives $\Sigma(F[k])\le1/t_H(F[k])$,
and \cref{prop:bridge} gives the reverse inequality.
head: environment

title: Lemma
head: environment
name: anticommutators bound traces

title: Proof
body_md:
The operator $X+YXY=(XY+YX)Y$ has the rank of $XY+YX$, norm at most $2$ and
trace $2\operatorname{Tr} X$.  The trace of an operator is at most its rank times its norm
in absolute value.
head: environment

label: eq:rank-ineq
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: rank inequality

title: Proof
body_md:
\emph{Completion.}  In each context, add the defect $I-S_c$ to one of its
four projections; in row $0$, add it to $P_0$.  Each context now carries four
orthogonal projections summing to $I$, labelled by its sign patterns.  For a
cell $(i,j)$, let $U_{ij}$ be the sum of the completed projections of row
$i$, each weighted by the sign it gives to the cell, and define $V_{ij}$ in
the same way from column $j$.  These are Hermitian unitaries.  The three
$U_{ij}$ in a row commute and multiply to $I$.  The three $V_{ij}$ in a
column commute and multiply to $I$, except in the last column, where they
multiply to $-I$.

\emph{Rows and columns agree off the defects.}  Fix a cell $(i,j)$.  Let
$U_\pm$ be the sum of the original projections of row $i$ that give the cell
the sign $\pm$, and $V_\pm$ the same for column $j$.  Two vertices that give
a shared cell opposite signs are non-adjacent, so $U_+V_-=U_-V_+=0$.  Let $z$
lie in the kernels of both defects, $I-S_i$ and $I-S_{3+j}$.  Then
$U_+z+U_-z=z=V_+z+V_-z$.  Put $x=U_+z$ and $y=V_+z$.  Then
$\langle x,z-y\rangle=\langle z,U_+V_-z\rangle=0$ and
$\langle z-x,y\rangle=\langle z,U_-V_+z\rangle=0$, so
\[
 \lVert x\rVert^2=\langle x,z\rangle=\langle x,y\rangle=\langle z,y\rangle=\lVert y\rVert^2 .
\]
Hence $\lVert x-y\rVert^2=0$ and $U_{ij}z=2x-z=2y-z=V_{ij}z$.  The two kernels meet
in a subspace of codimension at most $d(\delta_i+\delta_{3+j})$, so
\[
 \eta_{ij}:=\operatorname{rank}(U_{ij}-V_{ij})/d\le\delta_i+\delta_{3+j} .
\]
Put $e_j=\sum_i\eta_{ij}$ and $\varepsilon=e_0+e_1+e_2$.  Summing over the nine
cells gives $\varepsilon\le3\delta$, where $\delta=\sum_c\delta_c$.

\emph{Relations.}  Write $A,B$ for $U_{00},U_{01}$, write $D,E$ for
$U_{10},U_{11}$, and write $H,J$ for $U_{20},U_{21}$.  The $U$'s in a row
commute and multiply to $I$, so the last cells of the three rows carry $AB$,
$DE$ and $HJ$.  In column $0$, $V_{20}=V_{00}V_{10}=V_{10}V_{00}$.  Replacing
each $V_{i0}$ by $U_{i0}$ costs at most $\eta_{i0}$ in normalized rank, so
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(H-AD)/d,\ \ \operatorname{rank}(H-DA)/d\ \le\ e_0,
\]
and in the same way $\operatorname{rank}(J-BE)/d$ and $\operatorname{rank}(J-EB)/d$ are at most $e_1$.  In
the last column $V_{22}=-V_{02}V_{12}=-V_{12}V_{02}$, so
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(HJ+AB\,DE)/d,\ \ \operatorname{rank}(HJ+DE\,AB)/d\ \le\ e_2 .
\]
Since $HJ-AD\,BE=(H-AD)J+AD(J-BE)$, comparing $HJ$ with $AD\,BE$ and with
$-AB\,DE$ gives $\operatorname{rank}(ADBE+ABDE)\le d\varepsilon$.  Now $ADBE+ABDE=A(DB+BD)E$, and
$A$ and $E$ are unitary, so $\operatorname{rank}(BD+DB)\le d\varepsilon$.  In the same way,
$DAEB+DEAB=D(AE+EA)B$ gives $\operatorname{rank}(AE+EA)\le d\varepsilon$.  Finally, $A$ and $D$ lie
in column $0$, where $V_{00}$ and $V_{10}$ commute, so
$\operatorname{rank}(AD-DA)\le2d(\eta_{00}+\eta_{10})\le du_0$ with
$u_0=2(\delta_0+\delta_1+2\delta_3)$.  Likewise $\operatorname{rank}(BE-EB)\le du_1$ with
$u_1=2(\delta_0+\delta_1+2\delta_4)$.

\emph{Traces.}  By \cref{lem:anticomm}, $\lvert\tau(B)\rvert\le\varepsilon$ and
$\lvert\tau(A)\rvert\le\varepsilon$.  Since $A$ and $B$ commute, $AB$ is a Hermitian
unitary.  The identities $\{AB,D\}=A\{B,D\}+[D,A]B$ and
$\{AB,E\}=A[B,E]+\{A,E\}B$, together with \cref{lem:anticomm}, give
\[
 \lvert\tau(AB)\rvert\le\varepsilon+\min(u_0,u_1)\le\varepsilon+2(\delta_0+\delta_1+\delta_3+\delta_4).
\]
The completed row-$0$ projection with signs $(+,+,+)$ is
$\frac14(I+A)(I+B)$, and it equals $P_0+(I-S_0)$.  Taking normalized traces,
\[
 4\tau(P_0)+4\delta_0=1+\tau(A)+\tau(B)+\tau(AB)
 \le1+3\varepsilon+2(\delta_0+\delta_1+\delta_3+\delta_4).
\]
With $\varepsilon\le3\delta$ this is
$4\tau(P_0)\le1+7\delta_0+11\delta_1+9\delta_2+11\delta_3+11\delta_4+9\delta_5$,
which is~\eqref{eq:rank-ineq}.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $f(\alpha)=\log\vartheta_\alpha(G)$.

\emph{Right continuity at $\alpha_0\in[0,2)$.}  Pick a compatible family and
a faithful center whose order-$\alpha_0$ radius is at most $f(\alpha_0)+\varepsilon$.
For fixed states with a faithful center, $\alpha\mapsto D_\alpha$ is
continuous on $[0,2]$, including from the right at $0$, because
$\rho^\alpha\to\Pi_\rho$, and at $1$, where the limit is the relative
entropy.  So
$\limsup_{\alpha\downarrow\alpha_0}f(\alpha)\le f(\alpha_0)+\varepsilon$, and
monotonicity gives the reverse inequality.

\emph{Left continuity at $\alpha\in(0,1)$.}  Let $0<\beta<\alpha$ and
$\psi(t)=\ln\operatorname{Tr}\rho^t\sigma^{1-t}$.  By H\"older's inequality $\psi$ is
convex, and $\psi(1)=0\ge\psi(0)$.  So
$\psi(\beta)\le(1-\frac\beta\alpha)\psi(0)+\frac\beta\alpha\psi(\alpha)
\le\frac\beta\alpha\psi(\alpha)$.  Since both orders lie below one, this
rearranges to
\[
 D_\alpha(\rho\Vert\sigma)\le\frac{\alpha(1-\beta)}{\beta(1-\alpha)}
 D_\beta(\rho\Vert\sigma).
\]
The constant does not depend on the states or the dimension.  Applying it to
near-optimal witnesses at order $\beta$ gives
$f(\beta)\le f(\alpha)\le\frac{\alpha(1-\beta)}{\beta(1-\alpha)}f(\beta)$,
and the constant tends to $1$ as $\beta\uparrow\alpha$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For $s\ne0$ let $A=\sigma^s$ and $f(t)=t^{1/s}$.  For $s=0$ let $A=\ln\sigma$
and $f=\exp$.  In each case $f$ is convex on an interval containing the
spectrum of $A$ and
$f(A)=\sigma$.  Diagonalize $Q_jAQ_j$ on $\operatorname{ran} Q_j$ in an orthonormal basis
$(e_{jk})_k$.  Its eigenvalues are $\langle e_{jk},Ae_{jk}\rangle$, so
Jensen's inequality for the spectral measure of $A$ gives
\[
 Z_s(\sigma,Q_j)=\sum_kf(\langle e_{jk},Ae_{jk}\rangle)
 \le\sum_k\langle e_{jk},\sigma e_{jk}\rangle .
\]
The vectors $(e_{jk})_{j,k}$ are orthonormal, so the total is at most
$\operatorname{Tr}\sigma=1$.
head: environment

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label[lemma]{lem:exact-graph}
In~\eqref{eq:def-parameter}, \eqref{eq:cmin-def} and~\eqref{eq:sigma-def},
restricting to channels whose confusability graph is exactly $G$ does not
change the infimum.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Restricting can only increase an infimum, so we show the reverse.  Take a
compatible family $(\rho_x)$ on $\mathcal H$ with center $\sigma$ (or dominator
$T$).  If $E(G)=\varnothing$, every compatible family already has exact
confusability graph $G$, so there is nothing to prove.  Assume henceforth that
$|E(G)|>0$.  Add an orthonormal vector $f_e$ for each edge $e$ of $G$.  For a
vertex $x$ of degree $d_x>0$, let $\Pi_x$ project onto the $f_e$ with $e\ni x$,
and let $\Pi_E$ project onto all of them.  Put
\[
 \rho'_x=(1-\varepsilon)\rho_x\oplus\frac{\varepsilon}{d_x}\Pi_x,\qquad
 \sigma'=(1-\varepsilon)\sigma\oplus\frac{\varepsilon}{|E|}\Pi_E,\qquad
 T'=T\oplus\varepsilon\,\Pi_E ,
\]
and leave isolated vertices unchanged.  Adjacent $x,y$ now overlap on
$f_{\{x,y\}}$, while non-adjacent vertices share no new vector.  So the
confusability graph is exactly $G$.  Every Petz moment, relative entropy and
support weight splits over the two summands, and the new summand contributes
$O(\varepsilon)$.  So radii converge to the original ones as $\varepsilon\to0$.  Also
$T'\ge\rho'_x$ and $\operatorname{Tr} T'\to\operatorname{Tr} T$.  The statement for $C_{\min}$ follows from
the order-one radius identity.
head: environment

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label[lemma]{lem:preorder}
For graphs $G$ and $H$, the relation $G\le_*H$ of Li and Zuiddam, that is
$\overline G\overset{*}{\to}\overline H$, holds if and only if there are a
state $\omega$ and positive semidefinite operators $\omega_g^h$
satisfying~\eqref{eq:ea-sum} and~\eqref{eq:ea-orth}.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Apply the definition to $\overline G$ and $\overline H$.  A pair $\{g,g'\}$ is
an edge of $\overline G$ exactly when $g\ne g'$ and $g,g'$ are non-adjacent in
$G$.  A pair $\{h,h'\}$ is a non-edge of $\overline H$ exactly when $h=h'$ or
$h\sim h'$ in $H$, that is, when $h\simeq h'$.  The case $h=h'$ is included
because graphs have no loops.  So condition~(ii) for $\overline G$ and
$\overline H$ is~\eqref{eq:ea-orth}, and condition~(i) is~\eqref{eq:ea-sum}
with $\omega=\rho$.  Both conditions are homogeneous, so dividing $\rho$ and
every $\rho_g^h$ by $\operatorname{Tr}\rho$ makes $\rho$ a state.  (A nonzero $\rho$ is
implicit in the definition, since $\rho=0$ would relate every pair of graphs;
Li and Zuiddam note that $\rho$ may even be taken positive definite.  In
Cubitt et al.'s Definition~1, from which the definition is taken, $\rho$ is
the reduced state of a bipartite pure state, so it is a nonzero state
\cite[Definition~1]{CMRSSW2014}.)
Conversely, a state $\omega$ and operators $\omega_g^h$
satisfying~\eqref{eq:ea-sum}--\eqref{eq:ea-orth} satisfy (i) and (ii) with
$\rho=\omega$ in dimension $d=\dim\mathcal H$.
